\begin{abstract}
This teaching example shows how one R entry point generates the numerical
results, a vector figure and a LaTeX table used by a statistical manuscript.
Recompiling the paper after rerunning R updates every inserted result.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}

Reproducible statistical work keeps data processing, estimation and reporting
connected \citep{wickham2014}. Regression results should retain their modelling
assumptions and computational provenance \citep{gelman2020}.

\section{Methods}

We fit the teaching model \(\texttt{mpg} \sim \texttt{wt} + \texttt{hp}\)
to the built-in \texttt{mtcars} data. The R script writes all displayed results
to the project-local \texttt{outputs} directory.

\section{Results}

The analysis contains \SampleSize{} observations and has
\(R^2=\ModelRsquared\). The adjusted coefficient for weight is
\WeightEstimate{} miles per gallon per 1000 pounds.

\section{Limitations}

This small observational example demonstrates file flow rather than causal
inference. Diagnostics and subject-matter justification remain necessary.
